original_card.question: Can a legal decoder or coframe change improve the full signed moment, including changed helper targets?
methods: Construct and independently check one source-bound instance of the stated first experiment.
Seek an exact counterexample or target-specific complete-budget obstruction to that same proposed change.
original_card.acceptance_gate: A source-bound arbitrary-input identity and legal producer/consumer boundary with the complete paid and productive target invoice, including restoration, ownership, native alignment and extra charges. Price under the actual current model; historical ceiling.py assumptions must be established before use. A favorable optimistic relaxation keeps a route open but is not a completed supplier. A scoped local result remains useful; expansion requires the family-level budget gate.

first_step.inspect: Read revision 8, the selected review and live exact-source handoffs. Then follow this card's bounded first_experiment.
first_step.scope: Source-bound orientation only, not a supplier replay or theorem proof.

original_card.first_experiment: Price one complete changed itinerary with both paid and productive histograms. Check #5693/#5698 for overlap and their exact hypotheses before another coframe search. Use the signed invoice preflight where its boundary contract agrees; an inconclusive concave comparison is not a power crossing. Stop if an optimistic complete budget fails at the chosen target or native delivery remains unspecified.
original_card.bottleneck_link: Judge the actual current supplier contract and complete signed target/paid bill; frozen-profile ceilings require an applicability proof.
allowed_variations: One exact source head, helper/cut region or quantified proposition and changed hypothesis; check live handoffs first. Different seeds are not different scopes.
scope_change_triggers: Changing source head, helper/cut domain, operation alphabet or caller boundary without recording the new scope.
Treating an archived proposal or local numerical pass as complete supplier admission.

existing_checks.scope: Selected PR5599: complete helper-subspace construction and independent caller replay; five framework assumptions remain.
existing_checks.remaining: The next experiment must identify uncovered source-specific work. Successor archive intake does not transfer this admission.

actual_scope: Decoder code of the P104 local word: classify, over F_3, the 8-dimensional decoding codes on the 104 ports (vectors w_l with w_l[l] = 1 and zero on the 55 conflicting ports) that the owned deliveries of any legal word must span; show the code is unique up to coordinate signs with minimum weight 49, identify it with the carriers of PR5907 and the selected PR6030 word, and derive the scoped floor of 7 paid H1 per carrier (56 per call) for single-stage designs with an 8-dimensional partner code.
scope_change_reason: The card asks whether a legal decoder change can improve the full moment. In the local word the only paid mass not fixed by the contract is the owned descent of the carriers (56 per call on PR5907), and a cheaper decoder would need a different 8-dimensional code with lighter vectors. The question therefore reduces to classifying those codes; the result is an obstruction for that whole class, not a priced itinerary.
bottleneck_link: Each unit of owned descent per call is 18 units of rank-mass surplus on the PR5907 invoice (about 7.45e-5 in kappa). Theorem 3 with Lemma 4 shows that the 56 units per call cannot be reduced by re-shaping eight carriers on any code, so local-word savings must come from fragmentation of public and helper lifts or from designs outside the scope (partner codes of dimension >= 9, multi-stage relays).
stop_rule: Stop when the four certificate parts replay with exactly one solution in total and no free variable, the solution's row and column codes have minimum weight 49 and are sign-equivalent to the weight-52 delivery codes of both pinned words, f(7) = 36 is confirmed, and the three controls are rejected.

open_questions.question: Is there a legal word whose partner code has dimension 9 or more and whose carriers pay fewer than 56 per call in total?
open_questions.why_it_matters: It is the only single-stage escape from Corollary 5; PR6030 already has a 9-dimensional partner code through one bookkeeping direction.
open_questions.first_step: Extend code8.Model with a ninth basis vector outside the clique frame and enumerate codes in which some carrier vector has weight at most 36.
open_questions.blocked_by: The search space grows by the extra basis vector; no certificate yet.

open_questions.question: Can a multi-stage relay (partners receiving mixtures through public roles) reduce owned descent below 56 per call?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Corollary 5 bounds receivers only for direct deliveries; relays move the cost into public lifts, whose price must be compared.
open_questions.first_step: Price one relay of a single carrier with the exact invoice of the PR5907 word.

open_questions.question: Is there a computer-free proof that the E8 Gram code is the only 8-dimensional decoding code on these 104 root lines over F_3?
open_questions.why_it_matters: It would replace the certificate by an argument that extends to other port sets drawn from E8 root lines.
open_questions.first_step: Work in clique coordinates (PROOF.md section 5a): show that the cross-block conditions force every alpha_j to have full support on its S(3,4,8) block.
open_questions.blocked_by: Local subsystems of three blocks admit degenerate supports, so the argument has to be global.
